message.reasoning_content:
Let me work through this carefully.

The position: Aave V3 Ethereum Core, supplying ~$1,000 USDC, no debt. Venue risk matters. I can only propose an action.

Timeline of observations:

- O01 (2026-07-14T00:01): security_alert claiming active exploit at Aave V3 Ethereum Core, urging full withdrawal.
- O02 (2026-07-14T00:11): Correction — it was a planned internal test, no exploit, funds safe, withdrawal recommendation retracted. So O01 is resolved/false alarm. Only 10 minutes later. This is a retraction; the incident did not happen.
- O03 (03:00): onchain snapshot — normal utilization, USDC 91.09%, idle $190M. No reserves frozen except rsETH (frozen since April — pre-existing, not new).
- O04: governance — supply cap increase for stcUSD on MegaETH not proceeding. Not relevant to Aave V3 Ethereum Core USDC position.
- O05: onchain — USDT borrow cap raised. Normal governance ops.
- O06: governance — cap reductions executed. Normal ops.
- O07: governance — cap increases recommended (USDe etc.). Normal ops.
- O08: governance — Ether.fi Aave V4 whitelabel on OP Mainnet. Not relevant to this venue.
- O09 (23:35 on 14 Jul): one address withdrew $183.9M USDC; USDC utilization 100%, idle $0.09M, borrow rate 14% APR. BUT: same address withdrew ~$184M at same hour previous night and resupplied ~30 min later. So this looks like a routine large LP operational pattern (likely an institutional rebalancing or a known recurring withdrawal). The monitor itself flags the pattern as recurring. By O10 (12:00 on 15 Jul), idle USDC is back to $183M and utilization 91.4% — confirming resupply. So O09 was transient, resolved.
- O10: onchain — normal state, USDC idle $183M, utilization 91.4%.
- O11 (14:50 on 15 Jul, current time): Blockaid detected Ostium Vault exploit on Arbitrum, ~$18M USDC payout. Ostium is a different protocol on a different chain (Arbitrum). Does it touch Aave V3 Ethereum Core? The exploit is at Ostium's vault on Arbitrum. The attacker used forwarder/oracle reports to create artificial trade profit. This does not directly affect Aave V3 Ethereum Core. Unless Ostium uses Aave... no indication. ~$18M USDC payout from the vault — the vault's own USDC. No indication of contagion to Aave.

So the current state: no active incident at the venue. The earlier alert was retracted. Onchain metrics are normal-ish (USDC utilization 91.4% is somewhat high but with $183M idle liquidity, fine; the position is only $1,000 USDC supplied, no debt — supply-side risk in Aave V3 Core USDC is minimal; aave has bad debt socialization but USDC market is huge).

Risk assessment: low. The false alarm was corrected within 10 minutes. The large withdrawal was a recurring pattern and liquidity recovered. The Ostium exploit is on another protocol/chain, doesn't touch this position.

Action: hold. Exiting costs fees/slippage/lost yield and there's no need. No reason to reduce.

Wait — should I consider elevated due to the O01/O02 sequence? The alert was retracted authoritatively by the same source 10 minutes later, describing it as a planned internal test. That's a clean retraction. The onchain data since then shows normal operations, no freezes (except pre-existing rsETH), liquidity intact. So low risk, hold.

Could one argue "elevated" because a security desk issued a false exploit alert, indicating some confusion? The retraction says it was a planned internal test — the "exploit" transaction was a test. Funds safe. I think low is right. The position is tiny ($1k USDC supply on the largest Aave market). Even USDC utilization at 91-100% briefly doesn't threaten suppliers — suppliers can always withdraw as long as there's liquidity; idle dropped to $0.09M briefly at 23:35 but recovered by morning. Actually, during the window when idle was $0.09M, a supplier wanting to withdraw might have been unable to withdraw USDC fully... but that was ~12 hours ago and liquidity is restored ($183M idle). Current time 14:50 on 15 Jul, idle $183M at 12:00. So withdrawal is feasible now.

Ostium exploit: different venue, different chain. Not relevant. Don't react to noise/incidents that don't touch this position.

So: risk low, action hold.

Reasons:
- The earlier exploit alert at this venue was retracted by the same source as a planned internal test; no exploit occurred.
- Onchain metrics normal: USDC idle ~$183M, utilization back to 91.4% after a recurring large withdrawal/resupply pattern; no new freezes.
- The Ostium Vault exploit is on Arbitrum, a different protocol and chain; no observed linkage to Aave V3 Ethereum Core.
- Position is a small USDC supply with no debt; supply-side risk minimal; exiting would incur unnecessary costs.

Source ids: O02 (retraction), O09/O10 (liquidity pattern and recovery), O11 (unrelated exploit considered). Maybe include O01 too since it drove initial consideration but was corrected. I'll list O02, O09, O10, O11. Perhaps also O01 for completeness — the decision hinges on O01+O02 pair. I'll include both.
